title: Crime Scenes: Read the Danger, Protect the Evidence
next: Course complete — review any lesson from the list

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already size up every scene, use PPE, and call police when a scene isn't safe. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Read the warning signs of violence at vehicles, homes and on the street
  2. Know cover vs concealment, and how to get out
  3. Preserve evidence while you treat, and document for court

Textbook: Chapter 54, PDF pages 4384–4429
slides.say: Welcome to the final chapter of the course: crime scene awareness. As EMRs, you already size up every scene, use protective equipment, and call police when a scene isn't safe. As a PCP, you'll make more decisions on scene and write reports that may end up in court. Today we cover three things: the warning signs of violence at vehicles, homes and on the street; cover versus concealment, and how to get out; and treating a patient at a crime scene without destroying evidence. There's no BC protocol for this topic, so we'll finish with what the PCP actually does.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到本课程的最后一章：犯罪现场警觉。你们作为 EMR，早就会评估每个现场、使用防护装备，现场不安全时呼叫警察。作为 PCP，你在现场要做更多决定，写的报告也可能被拿上法庭。今天讲三件事：车辆旁、住宅里和街头的暴力预警信号；掩体和隐蔽物的区别，以及如何脱身；以及如何在犯罪现场救治病人而不破坏证据。这个主题没有 BC 流程，所以最后我们讲 PCP 实际上怎么做。

slides.title: No call is routine
slides.body:
• Shooting, stabbing, attempted suicide: expect violence
  • Any call: odd behaviour, threatening posture, harsh language
  • You may look like police: high-vis "PARAMEDIC" helps
  • Body armour: not always bulletproof; no head or neck cover
  • Rural: you may arrive long before police
  • Violence recognized → retreat and wait for police
slides.say: As an EMR you learned to size up the scene before touching the patient. As a PCP, do it on every call, for the whole call. A shooting, a stabbing or an attempted suicide warns you of violence. But any call can turn: watch for strange behaviour, threatening posture and harsh language, and move your team, and the patient if possible, to safety early. People often mistake paramedics for police, so high-visibility uniforms marked PARAMEDIC help. Body armour isn't always bulletproof and doesn't cover the head or neck. In rural areas you may arrive long before police. Once you recognize violence, retreat and wait for them.
slides.sayZh: 当 EMR 时你就学过：先评估现场，再接触病人。作为 PCP，每个呼叫都要这样做，而且贯穿整个呼叫。枪击、刺伤或自杀未遂，本身就在警告你有暴力风险。但任何呼叫都可能变味：留意反常的举动、带威胁的姿态和粗暴的言语，尽早把团队，能的话连同病人，一起转移到安全处。人们常把护理人员误认成警察，所以印有 PARAMEDIC 字样的高可视制服有帮助。防弹衣不一定防弹，也护不到头和颈。在农村地区，你可能比警察早到很久。一旦识别出暴力，就撤退，等警察来。

slides.title: Approaching a vehicle
slides.body:
• Park 6 m+ behind, 10° toward the driver's side, wheels turned left
  • Night: high beams and spotlight; never walk in front of the light
  • Tell dispatch the plate and location before you get out
  • Trunk shut? Move belly-in to the C column; watch the hands
  • Back seat occupied? Stop at C. Never pass the B column
  • Van: stay 3–5 m out; make contact 45° ahead of the A column
slides.say: A call about someone slumped over the wheel is riskier than it sounds; an impaired driver may think you're police. If you're first, park at least six metres behind, angled ten degrees toward the driver's side, front wheels turned fully left. At night, use high beams and the spotlight, but never walk in front of the light. Give dispatch the plate and location before you get out. Check the trunk is closed, then move belly-in to the C column and watch the hands. If the back seat is occupied, stop there. Never pass the B column into the kill zone by the driver's door. For a van, stay three to five metres out and approach forty-five degrees ahead of the A column.
slides.sayZh: 「有人瘫在方向盘上」这类呼叫比听上去危险，意识受影响的司机可能把你当成警察。如果你是第一辆车，停在目标车后至少六米，朝驾驶侧偏十度，前轮向左打死。夜里用远光灯和探照灯，但绝不要走到灯光前面。下车前先把车牌和位置报给调度。确认行李箱关好，然后侧身贴车移到 C 柱，盯住车里人的手。后座有人，就停在那里。绝不越过 B 柱，进入驾驶门旁的致命区。遇到厢式货车，要离车身三到五米，从 A 柱前方四十五度的位置接近。

slides.title: Entering a home
slides.body:
• One partner in front; the other back, ready to call for help
  • Listen for shouting; scan windows for weapons
  • Doorways are a fatal funnel: most bullets go through doors
  • Stand on the doorknob side; announce "Paramedics"
  • Let the person lead you; lights on; pick two exits
  • Gun or knife → back out; move scissors, bottles out of reach
slides.say: Homes can turn violent too: a patient waking up confused, or a frightened relative, can turn on you. One partner approaches; the other stays a short distance back, ready to call for help. Listen for shouting and glance through windows for weapons. A doorway is a fatal funnel: you're easy to see and hard to move, and most bullets pass through doors. Stand on the doorknob side, not the hinge side, knock and announce 'Paramedics' so no one mistakes you for police. Let the person who answers lead you, and ask for lights. Pick a primary and a secondary exit. See a gun or knife? Back out and call police. Move scissors and bottles out of reach.
slides.sayZh: 住宅现场也会突然变成暴力现场：刚醒来、意识不清的病人，或者受了惊吓的家属，都可能冲你来。一人上前，另一人在后面隔一小段距离，随时准备呼救。听有没有吵闹声，扫一眼窗户里有没有武器。门口是「致命漏斗」：容易被看见、难以躲开，而且大多数子弹都能打穿门。站在门把手一侧，不站铰链一侧，敲门并喊「Paramedics」，免得被当成警察。让开门的人带路，请他开灯。选好主出口和次出口。看到枪或刀？退出去，叫警察。把剪刀和瓶子挪到对方够不着的地方。

slides.q: You and your partner walk up to a house for an "injured person" call. Inside, a woman is screaming and a man is shouting threats. What should you do?
options: Knock from the doorknob side and announce "Paramedics"
Go in quickly before the patient is hurt worse
Send your partner around to the back door to look
Back away facing the house, stage somewhere safe, call police
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. You and your partner walk up to a house for an injured-person call. Inside, a woman is screaming and a man is shouting threats. What should you do? A, knock from the doorknob side and announce 'Paramedics'. B, go in quickly before the patient is hurt worse. C, send your partner around to the back door to look. D, back away facing the house, stage somewhere safe, and call police. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。你和搭档走向一栋房子，呼叫内容是「有人受伤」。屋里一个女人在尖叫，一个男人在大声威胁。你该怎么做？A，站在门把手一侧敲门，喊「Paramedics」；B，赶快进去，免得病人伤得更重；C，让搭档绕到后门去看看；D，面朝房子倒退离开，到安全处集结，呼叫警察。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is D. Screaming and threats mean the scene isn't safe. Back away while facing the house, so you'd see an attack coming, stage somewhere safe, and wait for police to secure it. A is the right way to knock on a safe call, but this isn't one. B can make you the next victim, and an injured paramedic makes the scene worse for everyone. C splits your crew and leaves no one watching your partner's back.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 D。尖叫和威胁说明现场不安全。面朝房子倒退离开，这样有人冲出来你能看见；到安全处集结，等警察控制现场。A 是安全呼叫时正确的敲门方式，但这次不是安全呼叫。B 可能让你成为下一个受害者，而受伤的护理人员会让所有人的处境更糟。C 把团队拆开，没人能照应你的搭档。

slides.title: Domestic calls: contact and cover
slides.body:
• Among the most dangerous calls; fight in progress → wait for police
  • Avoid words or moves that sound like a challenge
  • Your voice is your best tool: tone, pace, pitch
  • Contact: one partner treats the patient
  • Cover: the other gathers info, reads the room, warns early
  • Not a counsellor; learn your reporting duties
slides.say: Domestic disputes are among the most dangerous calls for police and paramedics. If a fight is in progress, wait for police. Emotions are already boiling, so avoid words or actions that sound like a challenge. Your voice is your best tool: the right tone, pace and pitch, with calm eye contact and body language. Many crews use contact and cover. The contact partner treats the patient. The cover partner gathers information, watches the tension, and warns at the first sign of trouble. Stay professional, however unpleasant it gets. Crisis counselling isn't your job, but you may have a legal duty to report domestic violence or child abuse, so learn the rules where you work.
slides.sayZh: 家庭纠纷是警察和护理人员面对的最危险的呼叫之一。如果正在打斗，就等警察。现场情绪早已沸腾，所以避免任何听起来像挑衅的话或动作。你的声音是最好的工具：合适的语气、语速和音调，加上平和的眼神和肢体语言。很多团队用「接触与掩护」分工：负责接触的人救治病人；负责掩护的人收集信息、观察紧张程度，一有苗头就提醒同伴。不管多难堪，都要保持专业。危机辅导不是你的工作，但你可能有法定义务报告家暴或虐待儿童，所以要了解你执业地的规定。

slides.title: Danger on the street
slides.body:
SceneWhat you do
Drug lab: cold pills, camp fuel, acids, booby trapstouch nothing; leave, with the patient if safe
Gangs: reputation, respect, retaliationno gang signs or slang; drive-by → load fast
Mass shootingstage until secure: up to 2 km out, away from window sightlines
slides.say: Some dangers come from the street. Clandestine drug labs, most often making methamphetamine, are full of flammable, toxic chemicals, and some cooks set booby traps. The only clues may be piles of cold medicine, camping fuel and strong acids. Touch nothing, leave, take your patient if it's safe, and let police and hazmat specialists secure it. Gangs live by three Rs: reputation, respect and retaliation, so never copy their hand signs or slang. After a drive-by shooting, load the patient quickly, so you're not a target for a second round. At a mass shooting, stay in staging until police secure the scene, possibly up to two kilometres away and out of sight of windows.
slides.sayZh: 有些危险来自街头。秘密毒品实验室，最常见的是制造甲基苯丙胺的，里面满是易燃有毒的化学品，有些制毒者还会设陷阱。唯一的线索可能只是成堆的感冒药、露营燃料和强酸。什么都别碰，撤离，安全的话带上病人，让警察和危险品专家去控制现场。帮派奉行三个 R：名声、尊重和报复，所以绝不要模仿他们的手势或黑话。飞车枪击之后，要尽快把病人抬上车，免得成为第二轮枪击的目标。遇到大规模枪击，在集结区等到警察控制现场；集结区可能远至两公里，而且要避开窗户的视线。

slides.title: Cover vs concealment
slides.body:
Cover: stops bulletsConcealment: only hides you
engine block and wheelsbushes, tall grass
curbs, dumpsters, utility polesdark shadows
solid oak desk, refrigeratorsofa, stuffed chair
brick or concrete-block walldrywall, cinder-block wall

Shooter above you? Engine and wheels. Not the fuel tank, not between the wheels (ricochet).
slides.say: This is the key idea of the chapter. Cover can stop a bullet: a vehicle's engine block and wheels, a curb, a dumpster, a utility pole, a solid oak desk, a refrigerator, or a brick or concrete-block wall. Concealment only hides you: bushes, tall grass, shadows, a sofa, or a drywall wall. A cinder-block wall looks solid, but its porous blocks may not stop a bullet. Hide behind concealment while you look for cover, and shape your body to it. If the shooter is above you, in a window for example, they can see over a car, so use the engine and wheels. Avoid the fuel tank, and don't hide between the wheels; bullets can skip off the pavement.
slides.sayZh: 这是本章的核心概念。掩体能挡住子弹：车辆的发动机舱和车轮、路缘、大垃圾箱、电线杆、实木橡木桌、冰箱，或者砖墙、混凝土砌块墙。隐蔽物只能把你藏起来：灌木、高草、暗影、沙发，或者石膏板墙。煤渣砖墙看着结实，但多孔的砖块未必挡得住子弹。先躲在隐蔽物后面找掩体，并让身体贴合掩体的形状。如果枪手在你上方，比如在窗口，他能越过车顶看到你，所以要躲在发动机和车轮后面。避开油箱，也别躲在两个车轮之间：子弹会从路面跳弹打到你。

slides.title: Getting out: retreat and self-defence
slides.body:
• Back away facing the threat; call for police
  • Give your unit number and location first; then the details
  • Interview stance: arm's length, 45°, knees soft, hands relaxed
  • Wrist grabbed? Pull against the thumb, then get away
  • Weapon raised? Throw your clipboard; run to the unit or cover
  • Force for defence only; document why you left
slides.say: When a scene turns bad, back away and call police, even if your partner is hurt; you can't help them if you're hurt too. Give your unit number and location first, so help comes even if you can't say more, then the attackers, injuries, weapons, vehicle and direction. On tense calls, use the interview stance: about an arm's length away, body at forty-five degrees, feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, hands relaxed. If someone grabs your wrist, don't jerk back; pull against their thumb, the weakest point, then get away. If a weapon comes up, throw your clipboard to make them flinch, and run. Use force only in defence, and document why you left.
slides.sayZh: 现场变坏时，倒退离开、呼叫警察，即使搭档受伤也一样；你自己也受伤就帮不了他。先报车号和位置，这样就算你来不及多说，支援也会到；然后再报施暴者、伤情、武器、车辆和离开方向。气氛紧张时用问诊站姿：离对方大约一臂远，身体成四十五度，双脚与肩同宽，膝盖微屈，双手放松。被人抓住手腕，别本能地往回拽；朝对方拇指方向抽，那是最弱的地方，挣脱后马上离开。对方举起武器，就把记录夹板扔过去让他本能地躲闪，然后跑。武力只用于自卫，并记录你撤离的原因。

slides.title: Preserving evidence while you treat
slides.body:
• Safety order: you → partner → patient → bystanders
  • Park where police say; bring in only the crew you need
  • Walk around casings, weapons, blood; first in? along the wall
  • Don't touch casings, phones, toilets or taps
  • Cut around bullet holes and knife cuts; never shake clothing
  • Tell police where you walked and what you moved
slides.say: Once police secure a crime scene, you go in to treat. The safety order is you, your partner, the patient, then bystanders. But you also owe the community: an intact scene helps police catch and convict the offender. Park where police tell you; they may be protecting tire marks, casings or blood. Bring in only the crew you need. Walk around evidence, away from the path the victim or suspect probably used; if you're first in, walk along the wall, because offenders usually leave by the shortest route. Don't pick up casings, use the phone, flush the toilet or run the taps. Cut around bullet holes and knife cuts, never shake clothing, and tell police where you walked and what you moved.
slides.sayZh: 警察控制犯罪现场后，你才进去救治。安全顺序是：自己、搭档、病人，然后是旁观者。但你对社会也有责任：现场保持完整，能帮警察抓到罪犯并定罪。按警察指定的位置停车，他们可能在保护轮胎印、弹壳或血迹。只带必要的人员进去。绕开证据走，避开受害者或嫌疑人可能走过的路线；如果你是第一个进去的，就沿着墙走，因为罪犯通常走最短的路线离开。不要捡弹壳、用电话、冲马桶或开水龙头。剪衣服时绕开弹孔和刀口，衣服绝不要抖，并告诉警察你走过哪里、动过什么。

slides.q: Police have secured a kitchen where a man was stabbed in the chest. As the PCP treating him, which action is correct?
options: Cut around the knife hole, set the shirt aside unshaken, and tell police
Cut straight through the knife hole; it's the fastest way to the wound
Rinse your bloody gloves in the kitchen sink before starting the IV
Put the knife in your kit so no one trips over it
slides.say: Let's try a scene decision. Police have secured a kitchen where a man was stabbed in the chest. As the PCP treating him, which action is correct? A, cut around the knife hole, set the shirt aside without shaking it, and tell police. B, cut straight through the knife hole, since it's the fastest way to the wound. C, rinse your bloody gloves in the kitchen sink before starting the IV. D, put the knife in your kit so no one trips over it. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道现场决策题。警察已控制一间厨房，一名男子胸部被刺伤。你是救治他的 PCP，哪个做法正确？A，绕开刀口剪衣服，衬衫不抖、放到一边，并告诉警察；B，直接沿刀口剪开，这样最快看到伤口；C，开静脉前，先在厨房水槽里冲洗沾血的手套；D，把刀放进你的急救包，免得有人被绊倒。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is A. You expose the wound without destroying evidence: cut around the hole, don't shake the clothing, because trace evidence can fall out, and tell police what you changed. B destroys the cut, which can show what weapon was used. C is on the list of things not to do, because running water can wash evidence away; change your gloves instead. D is wrong because police should secure weapons whenever possible; tell them where it is.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 A。暴露伤口时不要破坏证据：绕开破口剪，不抖衣服，因为微量证据可能掉出来，并告诉警察你改动了什么。B 毁掉了刀口，而刀口能说明用的是什么凶器。C 在禁止事项之列，因为流水会冲走证据；应该直接换手套。D 错，因为武器应尽量由警察保管；告诉他们刀在哪里就好。

slides.title: Document it for court
slides.body:
• Court may come a year or more later: your report is your memory
  • Record what you saw, what you heard, chain of custody
  • Scene facts: patients, supine or prone, where the weapon was
  • No conclusions, no exaggeration; note what the patient says en route
  • Clothing, medications → ED; weapons, ID, wallet → police
  • Print legibly; record why you left a scene
slides.say: You may be called to court to give testimonial evidence: what you saw and heard as a witness. Physical evidence is the objects and marks that tie someone to the crime. A trial may come a year or more later, so your report becomes your memory. Document what you saw, what you heard, and the chain of custody, meaning where each item went. Describe the scene: how many patients, supine or prone, where the weapon was. Write facts, not conclusions, and don't exaggerate. Record what the patient says on the way to hospital. Clothing and medications go to the emergency department; weapons, ID and wallets are best given to police. And print clearly.
slides.sayZh: 你可能被传上法庭提供证言证据，也就是作为证人讲你看到和听到了什么。实物证据则是把某人和罪行联系起来的物品和痕迹。审判可能在一年甚至更久之后，所以你的报告就是你的记忆。要记录所见、所闻，以及证据保管链，也就是每件物品的去向。描述现场：几个病人、仰卧还是俯卧、武器在哪里。只写事实，不下结论，也不夸大。记录病人在去医院路上说的话。衣物和药物交给急诊；武器、证件和钱包最好交给警察。还有，字要写工整。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
• Treats scene assessment as ongoing, start to finish
  • Plans en route: who approaches, who covers, where the exits are
  • Vague call? Asks dispatch for more; stages until police clear it
  • Hostile street: load first, treat in the ambulance
  • Full PCP toolkit, but changes the scene as little as possible
  • Hands over evidence and statements; reports as local law requires
slides.say: There's no BC protocol for crime scenes, so what changes for you as a PCP? First, scene assessment isn't a box you tick at the door; it continues until the call ends, because a safe scene can turn fast. Second, you plan more: en route, agree who approaches, who covers, and where the exits are. On a vague call like 'injured person', ask dispatch for more, and if in doubt, stage until police clear the scene. Third, on a hostile street, load first and do your interventions in the ambulance. You still use your full PCP toolkit, but change the scene as little as you can. Finally, hand over evidence and statements properly, and report as local law requires.
slides.sayZh: 犯罪现场没有 BC 流程，那作为 PCP，你有什么不同？第一，现场评估不是进门时打个勾就完事，它要持续到呼叫结束，因为安全的现场也可能瞬间变坏。第二，你要计划得更多：途中商量好谁上前、谁掩护、出口在哪里。遇到「有人受伤」这种含糊的呼叫，请调度多问些信息；拿不准时，就在集结点等警察清场。第三，在充满敌意的街头，先把病人抬上车，再在救护车里做处置。你照样用上全部 PCP 技能，但尽量少改变现场。最后，规范地移交证据和病人陈述，并按当地法律履行报告义务。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• More skills, more tunnel vision: look up between tasks
  • Scissors and sharps: keep them out of a patient's reach
  • IV naloxone (PCP only) acts in about 1 minute
  • Fast wake-up → withdrawal, agitation: ventilate first, start at 0.4 mg
  • Your interventions change the scene: tell police
  • The patient's words en route are evidence: write them down
slides.say: Now the watch-outs that are new at PCP level. More skills mean more tasks, and more tasks mean more tunnel vision, so look up between tasks and keep reading the room. Your kit holds scissors and sharps; keep them out of a patient's reach. In BC, only the PCP can give naloxone by IV, and by that route it works in about one minute. A sudden wake-up can bring withdrawal and agitation, so ventilate first and follow the BC steps, starting at zero point four milligrams. Every intervention changes the scene, so tell police what you moved or left behind. And anything the patient says during transport may become evidence, so write it down.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲 PCP 层面新增的注意事项。技能越多，任务越多；任务越多，越容易陷入隧道视野，所以每做完一件事就抬头，继续观察周围。你的急救包里有剪刀和锐器，要放在病人够不着的地方。在 BC，只有 PCP 能静脉给纳洛酮，这个途径大约一分钟起效。病人突然醒来可能出现戒断反应和躁动，所以先保证通气，并按 BC 的递增剂量给药，从零点四毫克开始。每一项处置都会改变现场，所以要告诉警察你动过或留下了什么。病人在转运途中说的任何话都可能成为证据，要记下来。

slides.title: Three things to remember, and to carry
slides.body:
1. Spot violence early, retreat: stop at C, never pass B, keep an exit
  2. Cover stops bullets; concealment only hides you
  3. Treat but change little; document saw, heard, chain of custody

Carry into PCP practice: safety first, the whole call · assess deeper, reassess after every intervention · know your BC scope exactly, and document it

Course complete — review any lesson from the list
slides.say: Three things to remember from today. One: spot violence early and retreat; stop at the C column, never pass the B column, knock from the doorknob side, and always keep an exit. Two: cover stops bullets, concealment only hides you. Three: treat your patient but change the scene as little as you can, and document what you saw, what you heard, and the chain of custody. Because this is our final chapter, here are three things to carry from EMR to PCP practice. First, safety comes first, on every call, for the whole call. Second, assess more deeply, and reassess after every intervention. Third, know your BC scope exactly: use every PCP tool when it's indicated, never one outside your scope, and document it all. Congratulations on finishing the course. Review any lesson from the list, and tap Ask if anything is unclear.
slides.sayZh: 今天记住三件事。一，及早识别暴力并撤退：在 C 柱停下，绝不越过 B 柱，站在门把手一侧敲门，始终留一条退路。二，掩体能挡子弹，隐蔽物只能藏身。三，救治病人，但尽量少改变现场，并记录所见、所闻和证据保管链。因为这是最后一章，再送你三件从 EMR 带进 PCP 执业的事。第一，安全永远第一，每个呼叫都是，而且贯穿整个呼叫。第二，评估更深入，每次处置后都要复评。第三，准确掌握你的 BC 执业范围：有指征就用上每一项 PCP 技能，范围外的一项也不碰，并全部记录下来。恭喜你完成本课程。可以从列表里复习任何一课，有不懂的点「Ask」。
